definition: The function being integrated: in $\int f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ it is $f(x)$.
A function whose derivative is the given function: $F(x)$ is an antiderivative of $f(x)$ when $F'(x) = f(x)$.
The $+\,C$ at the end of an indefinite integral, there because any constant differentiates to $0$.
A known value, such as $y = 5$ when $x = 2$, used to find the constant of integration.
An integral with limits, $\int_a^b f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x$. Its value is a number, not a function.
